title: Chest Thief
description: Bring danger to your storage with the Chest Thief — an outcast trader who steals your most valuable items and vanishes into the night. This mod adds a new hostile mob that sneaks into bases and villages, turning your loot into a constant risk.
body:
![Chest Thief mod - Steal & Disappear Into the Night!](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/33de8bb6e05dac5c071d2cf9c225dfddb87e6d81.jpeg)

**Your chests are being robbed. The thief doesn't vanish — it takes your loot to a real underground dungeon you can raid to get it back.** 
On a multiplayer server, everyone's                                                                                                                                           loot ends up in the same place — and whoever gets there first takes everything.                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  **Your base is a target.**                                                                                                                                                                                                       
  A thief spawns near player chests, steals at night, and disappears. The more you own,
  the more often it comes. Secure your base — or go on the offensive.                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  **Find the dungeon.**                                                                                                                                                                                                            
  Stolen items accumulate in a criminal base somewhere in your world, packed with loot                                                                                                                                             
  from every chest in the area. A Wandering Trader sells a map. Fight through the guards                                                                                                                                           
  and take it all — including what was stolen from your neighbours.                                                                                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  **Run your own operation.**                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  Kill the guards, mine their chest with a Silk Touch tool, and bring it home. Thieves                                                                                                                                             
  will start delivering stolen goods to you instead. On a multiplayer server, nobody                                                                                                                                               
  needs to know it's there.                                                                                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  **Use the thief as a spy.**                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  Put a lead on a captured Chest Thief and it will walk you toward the nearest chest it
  can find — a dungeon, a hidden cache, or another player's base they thought was secret.                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ## Compatibility                                                                 

  | | |
  |---|---|
  | **Fabric API** | Required |
  | **Cloth Config** | Optional — in-game config screen |                                                                                                                                                                          
  | **Xaero's Minimap** | Optional — waypoints for located bases |
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ---                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ## Configuration                                                                 

  Config files live in your Minecraft `config/` folder. They are created automatically on
  first launch. New fields added by mod updates appear automatically with sensible defaults
  — no manual migration needed. All values can also be changed via the Cloth Config                                                                                                                                                
  in-game screen.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                   
  ### `chest_thief_config.json`                                                                                                                                                                                                    
   
  **Spawning**                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                   
  | Field | Default | Description |
  |---|---|---|
  | `spawnWeight` | `20` | How common the thief is. Cows are 8 — higher means more frequent |
  | `spawnMinGroup` | `1` | Minimum group size when spawning |                                                                                                                                                                     
  | `spawnMaxGroup` | `2` | Maximum group size when spawning |
  | `spawnMinNearbyChests` | `2` | Minimum chests within detection range before a thief may spawn |                                                                                                                                
  | `spawnBiomes` | *(most overworld biomes)* | List of biome IDs the thief spawns in |                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  **Stealing**                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  | Field | Default | Description |                                                
  |---|---|---|
  | `chestDetectionRadius` | `100` | How far (blocks) the thief scans for chests |
  | `chestDetectionMaxVerticalDist` | `16` | Max vertical distance to a chest. Low values exclude buried dungeons |                                                                                                                
  | `chestInteractionIntervalTicks` | `60` | Ticks between steal attempts (20 = 1 second) |                                                                                                                                        
  | `maxCarrySlots` | `5` | How many item stacks the thief can carry before leaving |                                                                                                                                              
  | `stealOnlyListedItems` | `false` | If `true`, only items in `chest_thief_values.json` can be stolen |                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  **Combat**                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  | Field | Default | Description |                                                
  |---|---|---|
  | `panicChance` | `0.4` | Chance (0–1) the thief flees and drops an item when attacked |                                                                                                                                         
  | `panicDurationTicks` | `200` | How long the thief sprints away in panic (200 = 10 seconds) |                                                                                                                                   
  | `berserkDurationTicks` | `300` | Duration of berserk mode (300 = 15 seconds) |                                                                                                                                                 
  | `berserkSpeedMultiplier` | `1.5` | Speed multiplier during berserk (+50 % over base speed) |                                                                                                                                   
  | `berserkFollowRange` | `50.0` | Block radius the thief tracks targets during berserk |                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  **Stealth**                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  | Field | Default | Description |                                                
  |---|---|---|
  | `nightSpeedBonus` | `0.12` | Flat speed added at night on top of base movement speed |                                                                                                                                         
  | `stealthChance` | `0.85` | Chance (0–1) to go invisible when the cooldown expires |                                                                                                                                            
  | `stealthMinTicks` | `60` | Minimum duration of each invisible period (60 = 3 seconds) |                                                                                                                                        
  | `stealthMaxTicks` | `140` | Maximum duration of each invisible period (140 = 7 seconds) |                                                                                                                                      
  | `stealthCooldownMinTicks` | `200` | Minimum pause between invisible periods (200 = 10 seconds) |                                                                                                                               
  | `stealthCooldownMaxTicks` | `400` | Maximum pause between invisible periods (400 = 20 seconds) |                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  **Departure**                                                                    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  | Field | Default | Description |                                                
  |---|---|---|
  | `departDelayTicks` | `400` | Ticks the thief waits with a full inventory before leaving (400 = 20 seconds) |
  | `departDurationTicks` | `600` | Ticks the thief walks away before despawning — your last window to intercept |                                                                                                                 
  | `maxAgeTicks` | `48000` | Maximum thief lifetime before it departs regardless (48000 = 2 Minecraft days) |                                                                                                                     
  | `leavingSoundEnabled` | `true` | Whether the thief plays a smug sound while departing |                                                                                                                                        
  | `leavingSoundMinTicks` | `80` | Minimum interval between departure sounds (80 = 4 seconds) |                                                                                                                                   
  | `leavingSoundMaxTicks` | `160` | Maximum interval between departure sounds (160 = 8 seconds) |                                                                                                                                 
  | `leaveDurationTicks` | `200` | How long the thief walks away from a chest when its inventory is full |                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ---                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ### `chest_thief_values.json`                                                    

  A map of item ID → priority value. The thief always steals the highest-priority item                                                                                                                                             
  it finds in a chest.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ```json                                                                          
  {                                                                                                                                                                                                                                
    "minecraft:nether_star": 1000,                                                 
    "minecraft:elytra": 900,
    "minecraft:diamond": 500,
    "minecraft:iron_ingot": 200                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  }
  ```                                                                                                                                                                                                                              
                                                                                   
  Items not in the list get priority `1` and can still be stolen — the list only controls                                                                                                                                          
  what gets taken *first*. Set `stealOnlyListedItems: true` in `chest_thief_config.json`
  to restrict stealing to listed items only.                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                   
  Default priorities (highest to lowest): Nether Star, Elytra, Enchanted Golden Apple,
  Totem of Undying, Beacon, Netherite gear, Diamond gear, Gold, Iron, Ender Pearl, and more.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ---
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  ### `syndicate_config.json`                                                      

  **World generation**
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  | Field | Default | Description |
  |---|---|---|                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  | `baseSpacingChunks` | `32` | Grid cell size in chunks. Larger = rarer bases |  
  | `baseSeparationChunks` | `12` | Minimum distance from cell edge to base centre |                                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  **Guards**                                                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  | Field | Default | Description |                                                
  |---|---|---|                                                                                                                                                                                                                    
  | `guardArrowDamage` | `2.3` | Base arrow damage (vanilla skeleton = 2.0) |
  | `guardsPerItem` | `0.5` | Guards spawned per item in the base (rounded down) |                                                                                                                                                 
  | `minGuards` | `4` | Minimum guards regardless of loot count |                                                                                                                                                                  
  | `maxGuards` | `16` | Maximum guards regardless of loot count |                                                                                                                                                                 
  | `guardRespawnIntervalTicks` | `6000` | Ticks between respawn checks (6000 = 5 minutes) |                                                                                                                                       
  | `guardRespawnPlayerBuffer` | `8` | Buffer (blocks) around the base AABB that blocks respawn |                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  **Loot**                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
  | Field | Default | Description |                                                
  |---|---|---|
  | `starterLootTotal` | `10` | Items placed in the base at world generation |

title: AuthProxy
description: Allow Minecraft server do online authentication with user provided proxy.
body:
Allow Minecraft server use user provided proxy to do online authentication.

In some areas of the world, sometimes Mojang's server can't be connected easily. This mod allow users to use a proxy for authentication, to overcome this problem.

Usage:

- Install this mod only in your _server_. This mod doesn't apply on client, because Minecraft client has built-in proxy support.
- Set JVM properties `socksProxyHost` and `socksProxyPort` for SOCKS5 proxy, or `http.proxyHost` and `http.proxyPort` for HTTP proxy. For example, if your SOCKS5 server is at `127.0.0.1:1080`, you should add `-DsocksProxyHost=127.0.0.1 -DsocksProxyPort=1080` to your launch script.
- Start your server and enjoy! Your server log should show a line like `Use SOCKS/HTTP proxy: host:port`.

---

允许 Minecraft 使用用户指定的代理来完成用户验证。

在世界上的一些地方不能轻松地访问 Mojang 的验证服务器。这个 mod 允许用户使用一个代理来连接验证服务器，从而解决这个问题。

用法：

- 安装这个 mod 到你的 _服务端_ 。这个 mod 不适用于客户端，因为 Minecraft 客户端有着自带的代理支持。
- 设置 JVM 参数。如果你使用的是 SOCKS 代理，请设置 `socksProxyHost` 和 `socksProxyPort` 参数，或者如果你使用的是 HTTP 代理，设置 `http.proxyHost` 和 `http.proxyPort` 参数。例如，如果你的 SOCKS5 服务器在 `127.0.0.1:1080` 上，你应该添加 `-DsocksProxyHost=127.0.0.1 -DsocksProxyPort=1080` 到你的启动脚本中。
- 启动你的服务器，然后享受吧！你的服务器日志中应该会多出一行类似于 `Use SOCKS/HTTP proxy: 地址:端口` 的信息。

description: Minecraft mod that sends random messages on intervals.
body:
# IF YOU WANT THE MOD UPDATED TO NEWER/OLDER MC VERSIONS PLEASE MAKE AN ISSUE ON THE GITHUB. IT WON'T BE UPDATED IF I GET NO REQUESTS FOR IT.
# AFKAdvertiser
AFKAdvertiser is a Minecraft mod which sends a random chat message from a list on an interval.
## Dependencies
The mod depends on [Fabric-Api](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api).
## Configuration
To configure the mod, put the mod in your mods folder and launch the game. A txt file will be created in `.minecraft\config` named `afkadvertiser.txt`. This txt file will have the following contents by default:
```
60
10
First Line
Second Line
```
The first line is the interval in seconds between messages, the second is the random offest in seconds, all the following lines are the messages which are randomly selected, there can be an infinite number of messages (well, actually 2,147,483,647).
When in-game, toggle it with /afkadvertiser.
### Timing
How the mod internally works is that a task is run after `interval` seconds, this task then adds an extra random amount of seconds between zero and `random_offset` (a float, so not alligned to the second), after that extra time has elapsed, it sends a random message.
So the time between messages is `interval+random(0,random_offset)`.
## Issues
If you have issues or found a bug, create an issue on github.
## Contributing
If you want a feature to be added or want to add something yourself, please first open a feature request on github.

title: The Trial Maze
description: This mod turns the entire world into a Trial Chambers.
body:
This mod makes it so that the entire Overworld is replaced with a randomly generated maze of Trial Chambers. Be careful not to get lost! (_Hint: You can't avoid getting lost. It's inevitable._)

Chests with loot can occasionally be found around the world, giving you wood and pickaxes. In addition, large rooms (like the [Atrium](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Trial_Chambers_atrium_1_(1).png) or [Chamber 4](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Trial_Chambers_chamber_4.png)) generate randomly. Good luck!

<details>
<summary>Overworld Generation Details</summary>

Every structure that can generate in the Overworld is an edited version of one of the vanilla Trial Chambers rooms or structures. In addition to corridors, these rooms can spawn:

- [Atrium](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Trial_Chambers_atrium_1_(1).png)
  - _<small>In this room, the reliefs on the sides were removed, and the structure was made less tall by removing the walkways and vault at the top.</small>_
- [Chamber 4](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Trial_Chambers_chamber_4.png)
  - _<small>In this room, the walkways have been shifted to account for the opening positions. In addition, several new openings were added.</small>_
- [Slanted](https://minecraft.wiki/w/File:Trial_Chambers_slanted.png)
  - _<small>This room was barely edited (from a version I found in my world), except for the entrances being fixed.</small>_

</details>

<details>
<summary>Nether Generation Details</summary>

All of these structures were built myself after looking at a real fortress. There are many inaccuracies compared to real fortresses, but that's probably okay. Right?

In addition to open and closed corridors, these rooms can spawn:

- Lava intersection (with one square of lava in the middle). This room was not modified.
- Staircase with nether wart. This room was significantly compressed side-to-side to prevent it from being ridiculously large.

Open corridors can contain blaze spawners and closed corridors can contain chests (with loot identical to vanilla fortress loot).

</details>

NOTE: This mod is not finished! The End is not modified, and some more Trial Chambers rooms will be added soon.

title: Timer & Clock
description: This mod displays the current time and a customizable timer directly above the hotbar. It lets you keep track of time without interrupting your gameplay.
body:
This mod adds a clock and timer display directly above the hotbar, allowing players to always see the current time while playing. In addition, it features a fully customizable timer that can be used for challenges, speedruns, or reminders. This helps you manage your time efficiently without having to pause the game.

Commands:

- /timeset12 – switches the clock to the 12-hour format
- /timeset24 – switches the clock to the 24-hour format
- /timeup – starts a timer that counts up
- /timedown <time> – starts a countdown (e.g. 15h40m30s, 1h, 40m)
- /timepause – pauses the current timer or countdown
- /timeresume – resumes the paused timer or countdown
- /timestop – stops the current timer or countdown and shows the clock again

title: Tape
description: Ever wished, you had Adhesive Tape in the Game? If so, that's Mod for you! Adds various Adhesive Tapes to the Game.
body:
![Banner](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/e1017f9409460e88916a2dc11f32586b7820da57.jpeg)Ever wondered, what you'd do, if Adhesive Tape existed in the Game?
Wonder no more! 

**This Mod gives you the option to craft various types of Adhesive Tapes, that can be placed on floors, walls, ceilings in any combination imaginable. Simply right click on any solid surface with the tape in your hand.**

* Want to add markings around some Machinery? Use the Adhesive Tape (Hazard)
* Have to make sure, nobody wanders into your Reactor Room? Use the Radiation Hazard variant.
* And much more...

![gallery image](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/3972bb2c8d5c2c477bc914009d5c9b4e3924888e.jpeg)

This mod offers you the following items:
* **Blank Adhesive Tape** - it's the crafting ingredient for further variants. Crafted from one slimeball surrounded by paper.
* **Colored Adhesive Tape** - tape available in all colors of the game, crafted by surrounding a blank tape with the chosen dye.
* **Defective Machinery Tape** - crafted by alternating white and blue dye, stripe pattern.
* **Hazard Tape** - crafted from black and orange dye, stripe pattern
* **Protection Tape** - crafted from white and red, stripe pattern
* **Radiation Hazard Tape** - crafted from orange and purple dye, stripe pattern
* **Safety Tape** - made from white and green, checkerboard pattern
* **Guidance Tape** - crafted from black and white, checkerboard pattern

Additionally:
* Config options to disable the dyed or the pattern tapes (including ingame UI)
* Translations into english, german
* You can freely use this Mod in public and private Modpacks alike, the usual rules apply in terms of linking back etc.

## Incompatabilities
I don't think there are any, since it doesn't modify anything, it just extends existing stuff, but let me know if you find something.

If you want to contact me, feel free to join my [Matrix Community](https://matrix.to/#/#artifact:55bytes.io), and send a message into the appropriate Channels.

- Cloth Config
- PetarLib
- ModMenu (optional)

Download and place in your mods folder. Configure with your API credentials to start tracking!

title: Fabric Energy API
description: A API that provides a simple and standardized way to handle energy in Fabric.
body:
# Fabric Energy API

**Why?**

Very annoying that every modpack for Fabric uses its own library and reimplementation of a energy system, meanwhile forge has a standardized API that makes most (if not all) mods cross compatible, while Fabric is stuck with energy mods that need specific compatibility mods, and its just a general mess.

This project wants to solve that. By creating a simple, fast, and modern energy API to hopefully one day become the gold standard for fabric, making energy a standard and cross compatible spec. 

**How it works.**

We have a unit called Fabric energy (Or just FE for short), which is calculated every single tick, similar to how Forge energy works. (FE/t) 

For the API spec visit the github repo.

**Notes**

Users, this mod adds no actual content, its a API for developers.

For mod developers, this api is on both Modrinth and Curseforge, so no need to worry about platform exclusivity.

title: As Intended
description: Bringing the choice back to the player.
body:
![.](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/e32fbfb0d46dd007cf587452d1e6cb786ac797f2_0.webp)

> **As Intended** is built around Minecraft’s original design philosophy: a sandbox defined by player choice, not guided progression. Where many modern modpacks rely on quests and guided systems to create direction, this pack intentionally steps back, allowing gameplay to emerge naturally from exploration, experimentation, and personal goals.
> 
> **As Intended** aims to preserve the original Minecraft experience, _as Mojang intended_. There are no quests and no forced paths, only expanding features where needed and keeping mechanics that already work.

![.2](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/07e851af9977232f863a9c4b64cdb70d33045a51_0.webp)

> **As Intended** aims to preserve the vanilla gameplay while also expanding what's needed. The pack intentionally avoids mods that provide excessive guidance or external information. There are no minimap mods and no recipe viewers such as JEI, REI, or EMI.
> 
> Exploration and navigation rely on in-game tools, most notably the Antique Atlas. Crafting and progression are handled through the vanilla recipe book, encouraging discovery rather than instant knowledge.
> 
> Large-scale content mods that dramatically alter gameplay flow are intentionally excluded. Additions are limited to mods that complement existing systems, such as Farmer’s Delight, which expands farming and food in a way that feels consistent with vanilla design. Any included content is optional, non-intrusive, and never required to “progress”.

![.3](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/faf8cd4c685126480eadd5237ec2fab34027c5c3_0.webp)

> Performance is a core pillar of **As Intended**. Every update aims to improve or maintain performance across a wide range of systems, including lower-end hardware and servers.
> 
> The modpack prioritizes lightweight, well-optimized mods and avoids unnecessary overhead. Visual enhancements are carefully selected to remain performant; currently included shaders such as Visual Vibrance and Miniature Shader provide subtle visual improvements similar to Vibrant Visuals while maintaining high framerates.
> 
> No feature is included at the cost of stability or responsiveness. If a mod negatively impacts performance without offering meaningful gameplay value, it does not belong in **As Intended**.

| System | Settings | Avg. FPS |
|---------|----------|----------|
| Ryzen 5 5600, RX 6600, 10GB Allocated RAM, 1080p | 16 Render Distance | 140 |
| Ryzen 5 5600, RX 6600, 10GB Allocated RAM, 1080p | 32 Render Distance | 90 |
| Ryzen 5 5600, RX 9070 XT, 10GB Allocated RAM, 1080p | 16 Render Distance | 600 |
| Ryzen 5 5600, RX 9070 XT, 10GB Allocated RAM, 1080p | 32 Render Distance | 200 |


![.4](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/579a3c6d899df525992669f77ddab54f0bf0079b_0.webp)

> **As Intended** is not intended for players who prefer heavily guided gameplay. If you enjoy structured questlines, clear progression paths, or mods that provide constant direction and objectives, this pack may not be a good fit.
> 
> Players looking for large-scale tech systems, automation chains, or major gameplay overhauls may also find this pack too restrained. There are no complex machinery trees, no RPG-style leveling systems, and no content designed around optimization or endgame grinds.
> 
> This pack is also not focused on instant information. If you rely on minimaps, recipe viewers, or external overlays to play efficiently, **As Intended** deliberately moves away from that approach in favor of discovery, exploration, and player intuition.


![.5](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/362c70b6abb3ecb4397e09b6cc24466e11095e52_0.webp)
### Suffixes:
> - **None** - Base pack
> - DH - Base pack with Distant Horizons

**Note: All of these versions are compatible with each other server-wise. Also the numbering is the same for serverpacks**

title: AwesomeKeycards
description: AwesomeKeycards lets you turn any item into a digital keycard, lock interactive blocks, and share access with trusted players.
body:
# AwesomeKeycards

**Author:** NeonDev  
**Platform:** PaperMC 1.21.8  
**Language:** Kotlin (2.3.0-Beta2) using Gradle + Shadow + run-paper.  
**Version:** 1.4.1

AwesomeKeycards lets you turn any item into a digital keycard, lock interactive blocks, and share access with trusted players. It is designed for modern survival servers that want lightweight door/loot protection without relying on heavy land-claim systems.

---

## Feature Highlights

- 🔐 **Custom-labeled keycards** – `/keycard create [global|team <team>] <label>` converts the held item with a unique ID, plus optional color/style/auto-close/double/notify/cooldown presets.
- 🚪 **Block locking** – lock doors, trapdoors, fence gates, buttons, chests, barrels, furnaces, shulkers, etc. Only matching keycards (or shared users) can interact.
- 👥 **Shareable access** – card owners can grant or revoke access via `/keycard access add/remove/list`, perfect for roommates or faction mates.
- 🧩 **Flexible key types** – create personal (default), `global`, or `team <name>` keys to match open-access lobbies or scoreboard-managed squads.
- 🎛️ **Command presets** – set accent color, effect style, auto-close timer, double-door sync, owner alerts, and cooldown defaults right on the `create` command.
- 📦 **Admin vault** – `/keycard vault` lists every keycard with quick cloning and revoke options that also clean up locks.
- 👁️ **Lock inspection** – shift-right-click a locked block with any keycard to see its linked key, owner, and a copyable ID (admins only).
- 🚪 **Door customization** – `/keycard door` (owner, no admin perm) controls auto-close timers, double-door syncing, owner alerts, cooldowns, style presets, nicknames, and a copy/paste clipboard for fast setup.
- 🌈 **Style presets** – pick classic, stealth, or spark effects per lock to change particle colors and sounds.
- 🔔 **Owner alerts** – optional pings when someone uses your lock, throttled to avoid spam.
- ⏱️ **Use cooldowns** – rate-limit rapid spam on doors or buttons with a per-lock delay.
- 🧾 **Door status HUD** – instant summary of the targeted lock’s nickname and toggles via `/keycard door status`.
- 🗂️ **Config clipboard** – copy/paste lock settings between doors to set up bases quickly.
- 🎨 **Visual feedback** – particle trails + jingles on lock/unlock and a subtle denied tone when access is blocked.
- 💾 **Persistent storage** – locks saved to `locks.yml`, cards + ACL to `keycards.yml`, ensuring safety across restarts.
- ⚙️ **Fine-grained permissions** – admin-only workflow for creating/locking, but anyone with the access permission can manage sharing for their own cards.
- 🧠 **Team watchdog** – optional allow/deny lists plus automatic pruning of team keys tied to removed teams keep ACLs clean.
- 📜 **Audit log** – `/keycard audits` tail recent lock/unlock attempts with player, key short ID, and location.

---

## Commands

| Command                                                                                                                                                               | Permission                                                         | Description                                                                                                         |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `/keycard create [global/team <team>] <label> [color=<name>] [style=<preset>] [autoclose=<seconds/off>] [double=<on/off>] [notify=<on/off>] [cooldown=<seconds/off>]` | `awesomekeycards.admin` | Converts the held item into a labeled keycard with optional defaults for future locks. |
| `/keycard lock`                                                                                                                                                       | `awesomekeycards.admin`                                            | Links the held keycard to the block you are looking at (6 block reach).                                             |
| `/keycard unlock`                                                                                                                                                     | `awesomekeycards.admin`                                            | Unlocks a block if you hold the linked keycard.                                                                     |
| `/keycard access add <player>`                                                                                                                                        | `awesomekeycards.access`                                           | Grants another player the ability to use the current keycard.                                                       |
| `/keycard access remove <player>`                                                                                                                                     | `awesomekeycards.access`                                           | Revokes access for a player.                                                                                        |
| `/keycard access list`                                                                                                                                                | `awesomekeycards.access`                                           | Lists everyone who can use the current keycard.                                                                     |
| `/keycard view`                                                                                                                                                       | `awesomekeycards.access`                                           | Displays owner, scope, and sharing details for the held keycard.                                                    |
| `/keycard door <status/autoclose/double/notify/cooldown/style/nickname/copy/paste>`                                                                                   | `awesomekeycards.access` (owner or admin)                          | Customize the targeted locked block: timers, double-door syncing, alerts, styles, nicknames, and clipboard actions. |
| `/keycard vault [page]`                                                                                                                                               | `awesomekeycards.admin`                                            | Browse all stored keycards, clone them, or revoke + clean locks.                                                    |
| `/keycard audits [player] [count]`                                                                                                                                    | `awesomekeycards.admin`                                            | Show the most recent audit lines; defaults to 10 entries.                                                           |

> Hold the keycard item in your main hand before running any command.  
> By default `awesomekeycards.admin` is OP-only, while `awesomekeycards.access` is granted to all players so they can manage their own cards.

Example: `/keycard create global Lobby color=gold style=sparks autoclose=5 double=off notify=on cooldown=3`

---

## Supported Blocks

- All **doors**, **trapdoors**, **fence gates**, and **buttons** (via Bukkit tags).  
- Utility blocks: levers, barrels, chests (normal & trapped), furnaces, smokers, blast furnaces, droppers, dispensers, hoppers, shulker boxes (all colors).  
- When locking double-doors, aim at the lower half; the plugin normalizes coordinates so both halves stay linked and, if enabled, will sync open/close on both sides.

---

## Keycard Types

- **Personal** – default behavior. Owner plus manually shared UUIDs can operate linked blocks.  
- **Global** – `/keycard create global <label>` lets every player interact with blocks locked to that key (great for spawn doors that still log activity).  
- **Team** – `/keycard create team <teamName> <label>` ties the lock to a vanilla scoreboard team (`/team add Guards`). Any member of that team can open the block without needing the physical item.  

Use `/keycard view` while holding a card to confirm its scope, owner, and share list before distributing copies.

---

## Door Customization (no admin needed)

Owners (or admins) looking at a locked block can run `/keycard door ...`:
- `status` – show nickname plus all toggles for the targeted lock.
- `autoclose <seconds|off>` – close doors/fence gates/trapdoors automatically after a delay.
- `double <on|off>` – open/close both halves of a double door together.
- `notify <on|off>` – ping the owner when others use the lock (throttled).
- `cooldown <seconds|off>` – add a short delay to prevent spammy toggling.
- `style <classic|stealth|sparks>` – change particles/sounds per lock.
- `nickname <name|off>` – friendly label shown in status/alerts.
- `copy` / `paste` – clone all these settings between locks to set up bases quickly.

Defaults you set on `/keycard create` (color, style, auto-close, double-door, alerts, cooldown) are saved on the keycard and applied to locks the next time you link that card to a block.  
All customization uses the `awesomekeycards.access` permission (default true) and only requires owning the key, not server admin.

---

## Configuration

- `teamAccess.allow` / `teamAccess.deny` (lists) gate which scoreboard teams can be used for team keycards; leave `allow` empty to allow all by default.
- `teamAccess.watchdogIntervalTicks` controls how often stale/blocked team keycards are pruned.
- Audit logs are written to `plugins/AwesomeKeycards/audit.log` and can be tailed in-game with `/keycard audits`.

title: Daily AutoRestart
description: Automatically restart your server daily at a scheduled time with customizable warnings
body:
# Daily Auto Restart

Automatically restart your server daily at a scheduled time with customizable warnings

![Minecraft](https://img.shields.io/badge/Minecraft-1.13--1.21.1-brightgreen) ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/Version-1.0.3-blue) ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow) ![Downloads]

---

## Overview

DailyAutoRestart is a lightweight, reliable plugin that automatically restarts your Minecraft server at a specific time each day. Unlike interval-based restart plugins, this uses actual time-of-day scheduling, ensuring consistent restart times regardless of when your server started.

Perfect for server maintenance, reducing lag buildup, and keeping your server running smoothly!


---

## Features

- **⏰ Scheduled Daily Restarts** - Set exact restart time in 24-hour format
- **⚠️ Multiple Warning Levels** - Warns players at 60, 30, 15, 5, and 1 minute before restart
- **⏱️ 10-Second Countdown** - Dramatic countdown from 10 to 0 before restart
- **🔊 Sound Notifications** - Optional sound effects for warnings (fully configurable)
- **🎨 Fully Customizable Messages** - All messages support color codes and placeholders
- **🔄 Live Reload** - Update settings without restarting the server
- **🛡️ Permission System** - Control who can view info and reload config
- **📊 Utility Commands** - Check server time and time until restart
- **🔔 Update Checker** - Automatic notifications when new versions are available
- **🪶 Lightweight** - Minimal performance impact
- **🔧 Easy Configuration** - Simple YAML configuration

---

## Commands

| Command | Aliases | Description | Permission |
|---------|---------|-------------|------------|
| `/dailyautorestart` | `/dar`, `/dailyrestart` | View restart info and help | `dailyautorestart.use` |
| `/dailyautorestart reload` | - | Reload configuration | `dailyautorestart.reload` |
| `/servertime` | `/stime`, `/time` | Display current server time | `dailyautorestart.use` |
| `/timeuntilrestart` | `/untilrestart`, `/restarttime` | Show time until next restart | `dailyautorestart.use` |

---

## Perms

- **`dailyautorestart.use`** - View restart info and use utility commands (default: true)
- **`dailyautorestart.reload`** - Reload plugin configuration (default: op)
- **`dailyautorestart.updatenotify`** - Receive update notifications (default: op)

title: More Recipes: Craft Gilded Blackstone
description: Craft Gilded Blackstone from Blackstone & Gold Nuggets.
body:
Recipe downloads have been split into their own projects for better Modrinth App compatibility.\
Links to all recipes in description

This project adds renewable Gilded Blackstone by making it craftable from Blackstone and 4 Gold Nuggets (the average drop from Fortune III on Gilded Blackstone). While technically possible to use this to make more gold, it is highly inefficient.


#### Installation:
- Put the datapack in your "/AppData/Roaming/.minecraft/saves/[Your World Here]/datapack" folder.
- ***DO NOT put the datapack in your "/AppData/Roaming/.minecraft/resourcepacks" folder.***
- If you changed where Minecraft loads from, find that location and use that "saves" folder.
- For servers, put it in your world folder that matches where your server.properties file says.

#### For advanced users:
- IF you want to store it in your ".minecraft" folder, CREATE a folder called "datapack" and put it there.
- From there, when you create a world and go to add datapacks, you can simply go to this folder and grab what you need.
- For identical recipes in multiple data packs, load desired recipes AFTER their duplicates


#### Datapack version reference (as of 1.21.10):

Datapack version is formatted as A.B.C
- A marks breaking changes to how the data pack is written
- B marks changes in either the "Pack Format" version or the game version itself (major update)
  - Special Note: as of 5.5.0 (1.21.9), pack formating now has minor versions. All minor versions for any given major versions are intended to fully compatible (i.e. - 88.0, 88.1, etc.) and listed as only the major version (i.e. - 88).
- C marks minor changes or fixes

The different release versions of "More Recipes by Selah":
- More Recipes: A balance of Quality of Life recipes while still feeling Vanilla
- Mini-Collections: Every recipe in "More Recipes" sub-divided into seven (7) categories
  - Additional, Change, Color, New, Smelting, Stonecutting, Undo
- Alpha: Every recipe divided into sub-categories based on the Mini-Collection categories
  - This is effectively the test version of all recipes
  - This is where recipes not in the Mini-Collection or comprehensive releases are
  - Feedback encouraged to bring as many recipes into the comprehensive release as possible

Datapacks were not a thing before 1.13. There is no way to make these compatible older than 1.13.

There are special cases where breaking changes that are not backwards compatible don't have the "A" value incremented:
- Item names are changed
  - ex: 1.1.x changes "rose_red" to "red_dye"
- A non-breaking functionality is added
  - ex: 2.6.x in 1.19.3 adds categories while anything before ignores them
- A change is made that doesn't stop the previous method from working
  - ex: "crafting_shapeless" works in all versions, "minecraft:crafting_shapeless" starting in 1.1.x
- Changes to the way "pack.mcmeta" is read
  - ex: see changes in 25w31a

title: Unseen
description: Hides players' visibility in chat, tablist, and social interactions.
body:
# Unseen

**Unseen** keeps players hidden until they're close enough to each other. It blocks tablist visibility, silences join/quit/death messages, and removes tab completion to keep sneaky vibes strong

**Note:** OP players can see everyone from any distance and remain invisible to non-OP players regardless of range.

---
<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/jL-4TwIlHkU" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>
---

## Features
- Players only see each other within a configurable distance (default 20 blocks)
- Suppresses join, quit, and death messages for stealth vibes
- Disables player name tab completion in chat so no spoilers
- Keeps the online player list a secret unless you physically spot 'em

---

## Dependency
- [ProtocolLib 5.4.0+](https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/protocollib.1997/)

---

## Installation
1. Download the latest release of **Unseen** & **ProtocolLib**
2. Place the `.jar` files in server's `/plugins` folder
3. Restart your server
4. Configure settings via `/unseen` commands or `config.yml`

---

## Commands (OP only)
- `/unseen distance <number>` - Set visibility distance
- `/unseen joinmessage` - Toggle join messages on/off
- `/unseen leavemessage` - Toggle leave messages on/off
- `/unseen deathmessage` - Toggle death messages on/off
- `/unseen reload` - Reload plugin config
- `/unseen help` - Show help message with commands

---

## Credits
**Plugin Author:** [nobstergo](https://github.com/nobstergo)  
**Contributor (Idea, Testing, Feedback):** [alprny](https://github.com/alprny)

---
If you want your server to get that sneaky *unseen* edge, this plugin got you covered! 😎

title: ItemPro
description: ItemPro - Because knowledge is power, even in Minecraft! ⚔️📚✨
body:
# ItemPro

**Advanced item information panel for Minecraft.** ItemPro enhances your inventory experience by providing detailed information about items directly in the game.

## Features

### 🏷️ Item Information Panel
- **Category**: Shows what type of item it is (Weapon, Tool, Armor, etc.)
- **Origin**: How to obtain the item (Crafting recipe, Drop location, etc.)
- **Description**: Detailed explanation of the item's purpose and stats
- **Enchantments**: Lists all enchantments with their levels

### 📱 Smart Display
- **Responsive Design**: Panel adapts to screen size and inventory position
- **Clean Layout**: Modern UI with rounded corners, shadows, and color-coded sections
- **Text Wrapping**: Long descriptions automatically wrap to fit the panel
- **Clipping Protection**: All text stays within panel boundaries

### 🔍 Detail View
- **Press G** while hovering over an item to open the detailed view
- **Full Information**: Complete item details in a scrollable window
- **Large Icons**: Items displayed prominently for easy identification
- **Comprehensive Data**: All categories, origins, and descriptions in one place

### 📚 Extensive Database
- **60+ Items Supported**: From basic tools to rare treasures
- **Vanilla Items**: Swords, armor, tools, materials, blocks, and special items
- **Detailed Entries**: Each item has category, origin, and description
- **Regular Updates**: Database grows with new Minecraft content

## Installation

1. **Install Fabric Loader** for Minecraft 1.21.10
2. **Install Fabric API** (required dependency)
3. **Download ItemPro** from Modrinth
4. **Place the jar file** in your `mods` folder
5. **Launch Minecraft** and enjoy!

## Dependencies
- **Fabric API**

title: Vanilla Spice Visuals
description: Enhances vanilla Minecraft by adding some block variants, a few 3D models, and retexturing lackluster blocks!
body:
<u>Vanilla Spice</u> is a resource pack that is basically just a texture pack but with a few 3D models and block variants. It aims to keep the overall _vanilla_ vibes of Minecraft by leaving most textures alone, but _spices_ it up by retexturing/remodeling some lackluster blocks. 

Compatible with **1.14 to 1.21.10**. Minecraft may say it is "Incompatible" for any version other than 1.21.8, but it should still work.

This resource pack includes:

**<u>Variants for:</u>**

- <u>short grass</u> (shorter short grass, sparser short grass, vanilla short grass, clovers, clover flowers, and 3D pebbles!)
- <u>bookshelves</u> (a variety of textures with different probabilities to make large bookshelves look more organic; slightly fancier style to suit enchantment rooms and library builds)
- <u>mushrooms</u> (small, medium, large, extra large, and cluster variants for both brown and red mushrooms; prettier designs in general; to compliment giant mushrooms, brown mushrooms have flat caps and red mushrooms have fuller caps with white scales)

**<u>3D models for:</u>**

- <u>ladders</u>! (still very vanilla in texture, just 3D)
- <u>minecart rails</u>! (also vanilla in style, just 3D)
- <u>pebbles</u> (technically a short grass variant; uses stone's texture)

**<u>Remodeled:</u>**

- <u>fences</u> (unique 3D models for each color fence to add variety; nether brick fences are modeled after wrought iron fences for victorian/goth builds)
- <u>fence gates</u> (swing open at one hinge rather than being double doors, unique gate doors with custom textures designed after their respective door/trapdoor textures)

**<u>Retextured:</u>**

- <u>andesite, diorite, granite</u> (and their polished versions to be more visually interesting and accurate to real life; polished diorite and granite are designed to work well as marble in builds)
- <u>stained glass</u> (much more vibrant colors, sectioned into leaded panes to give a more traditional stained glass look; panes based on redstone lamps; clear glass has the same shaped panes but in vanilla white colors for a more vanilla feel)
- <u>resin blocks</u> (including bricks and clumps, are given a more realistic deep amber color and shading, rather than flat orange)
- <u>iron block, iron door, iron trapdoor</u> (deeper metallic grey color to better represent real iron; block has studs like copper; iron door retextured to suit a larger variety of builds)
- <u>iron bars, copper bars</u> (more resemble old fashioned elevator gates rather than prison bars)
- <u>lanterns</u> (have a wire grate to fit the vibes of the stained glass and iron blocks)
- <u>carpets</u> (subtle knitted/braided texture; added fringe to model; slightly warmer colors)
- <u>bricks</u> (slight variation in color for each brick to make them less uniform)
- <u>mud bricks</u> (slightly more grey with a different brick pattern to allow for versatile role in builds)
- <u>red nether bricks</u> (fishbone brick pattern with brick color variation, also to allow for a more versatile role in builds)
- <u>glowstone</u> (has a warmer glow from within and compliments netherrack better)
- <u>rain</u>! (and rain particles to be whiter and more transparent for softer rain showers)

**<u>Tweaked:</u>**

- <u>iron chain</u> (recolored to match the leading in stained glass)
- <u>chiseled bookshelves</u> (wooden sides better match normal bookshelves/oak planks)
- <u>nether bricks</u> (copied the small brick layer for the top brick layer to allow brick pattern to interlock correctly)

**<u>Possible future updates:</u>**

- leaf litter variety (could be just in color of leaves, or also textures)

**<u>Notes:</u>**

Optifine is <u>not</u> necessary; this pack should work with or without shaders.

Again this texture pack should work for Minecraft versions 1.14 through 1.21.10, just bypass the "incompatible" warning by clicking yes; worst case senario is some textures/models are broken and you can just put this texture pack back on the "available" side. 

I do plan on making a Bedrock version of this pack, but it may take a while.

If you prefer certain vanilla textures over mine, feel free to delete mine from the pack folder, just don't upload my altered pack as your own. 

Likewise do not use any of my textures or models in your own resource pack. Of course I don't own things like 3D ladders or clover grass variants, but <u>just don't copy paste</u>.

title: Liminal Paintings

body:
### Warning/Note

If you download the datapack version, a resourcepack is **required**! If you are planning to use the datapack version, please manually go into the versions tab, choose the version you want, and download BOTH of the TWO attached files! The main one will be the datapack itself, and the "additional" one is the resourcepack required! If you do not do this, all paintings will have no defined texture and turn into pink and black checkerboard patterns!

**All links in the sidebar are DyoudiM!'s links, and are not related to me in any way.**

---

***DyoudiM!'s liminal-vibe artwork added to Minecraft as paintings!***

Currently there are **69** paintings added.
*(That number is NOT intentional, it is a coincidence)*

For **datapack** versions **below** 1.2.30:
To check credits in-game, you can use `/function tbdlp:credits`.
To give yourself ALL the paintings, use `/function tbdlp:all`.

For **datapack** versions 1.2.30 or **over**:
To check credits in-game, you can use `/function liminalpaintings:credits`.
To give yourself ALL the paintings, use `/function liminalpaintings:all`.

All credits for the artworks go to **[DyoudiM!](https://x.com/DyoudiM)**.

---

### Versions
- **Datapack** version: Includes a Datapack & a Resourcepack.
- **Custom Paintings** version: Includes a Custom Paintings pack that requires the [Custom Paintings mod](https://modrinth.com/mod/custom-paintings-mod). `Modloader will say Datapack, although it's not. It does not have a resourcepack option as the first uploaded version was a datapack.`

### Installation
To install the **datapack** version, first go into the versions tab, choose your version (must be labeled with "Datapack") and download **both** files attached, one is the datapack, the other (labeled "Resources" and is "additional") is a resourcepack.
Put the resourcepack in your resourcepack folder like normal.
Put the datapack in the "datapacks" folder in your already-existing world, or if it's a new world, add it during world creation.

To install the **custom paintings** version, first go into the versions tab, choose your version (Must be labled with "Custom Paintings") and download the file. Next make sure you have the Custom Paintings mod installed. If not, download it at [https://modrinth.com/mod/custom-paintings-mod](https://modrinth.com/mod/custom-paintings-mod).

To add the custom paintings pack to your world, you can follow the tutorial in the page's description ([https://modrinth.com/mod/custom-paintings-mod](https://modrinth.com/mod/custom-paintings-mod)).

Simply press `U` or whatever key you have set for opening the Custom Painting's mod menu **while in a world**. Then choose to manage packs, open the folder, and put the file into the folder. You can now close the folder, return to the game and choose to reload packs, ensure that the pack is listed, and done!

---

title: SimpleSilkSpawners
description: Simple to use, easy to install, bare bones Silk Spawners plugin for paper & Spigot.
body:
**Simple Silk Spawners**
**✅ Simple. Lightweight. No dependencies.**

Simple Silk Spawners is an easy-to-install plugin that enables players to collect mob spawners using Silk Touch. Perfect for survival servers that want a straightforward, no-fuss solution.

**Features**
Silk Touch Spawner Drops
Break any spawner with a diamond or netherite pickaxe enchanted with Silk Touch to collect it.
No configuration required, just install and go!
⚒️ Spawner Retrieval Command
Use /getspawner <type> to obtain any spawner type instantly (requires permission).
Simple Permissions
Silk Touch Permissions:
silkspawners.type.<type>
Allows a player to collect spawners of a specific entity type (e.g., silkspawners.type.zombie).
Get Spawner Permissions:
silkspawners.get.<type>
Allows a player to use /getspawner <type>.
No dependencies
No extra libraries, no configuration files – plug and play.
Commands

**Command Description**
/getspawner <type> Give yourself a spawner of the given entity type.
⚙️ Installation
Download the plugin .jar file.

Place it into your server's /plugins folder.

Restart or reload your server.

Enjoy!
Example Usage
To get a Zombie Spawner:

/getspawner zombie

(Requires silkspawners.get.zombie permission)

To allow a player to collect Skeleton Spawners with Silk Touch:

silkspawners.type.skeleton
**Supported Versions**
✅ Compatible with Spigot and Paper 1.21.5+

Simple Silk Spawners – Keep it simple. No clutter. Just functional Silk Touch spawner drops.

A simple data pack that configures the Cold Sweat mod to better work with Big Globe's expanded world height, overhauled biomes, and unique blocks.

Specifically, this datapack increases the altitude based temperature system to function logically both above ground and below, making the core very hot, and mountain tops rather cold. It also makes the added soul blocks (magma and lava) cold, as well as the molten rock blocks increasingly hot, and smooths the transitions in temperature between adjacent biomes.

Note that since Big Globe is only on fabric and Cold Sweat is on Forge / NeoForge, you will need to use something like Sinytra Connector to play the two together.

# Armor Begone

Armor Begone is a project I've been waiting for for 3 years that I finally decided to create. For Hypixel Skyblock players at a top level, outside of various cosmetics to add to your armor, nothing showcases your personality better than your skin.

I'm here to fix that.

## What does it do?

Essentially, any armor or player head (textured skull item) worn by the player will not render, allowing for a full view of other player's skins in game.

![BeforeEnabling](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/04e673514b21f47c2a2b3f09b5e36434d8e9171f_0.webp)

![AfterEnabling](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/d01d6eeb02cb1cbbc78d07238ad1147a7caf7292_0.webp)

## The Future

I am currently only going to be supporting fabric for 1.21.1 for the time being. From what I know of this is the best version of the game to be running mods for Hypixel Skyblock on that will be supported come the foraging update.

This is also my first mod, so realistically it's gonna take me a while to get the ball rolling :p

### Issues:

title: Aerial Combat
description: Aerial Combat adds a togglable combat mode where attacks hit mobs upward; the player has infinite jumps to increase air time, plus additional combat options.
body:
![Aerial Combat Title](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/c8094a53819b25cb0ad06006a47580483a3cd621.png)

## Features
B+ Aerial Combat adds many features and mechanics to set PVP/PVE airborne. 

<details>
<summary>Aerial Combat Mode</summary>

- The "Aerial Combat Mode" is toggleable (LEFT CONTROL by default) to keep the default Minecraft mechanics available when "Aerial Combat Mode" is unfavorable. Text will show above the hotbar, indicating whether it is on or off. (Aerial Combat: ON or Aerial Combat: OFF)

- While "Aerial Combat Mode" is enabled, the player will not take fall damage as it is very easy to die after a mid-air combo.

- While "Aerial Combat Mode" is enabled, the player has infinite air jumps (SPACE by default) to keep them in the air. This emits particles.

- "Aerial Combat Mode" is independent of "Auto Lock Mode" to allow players to use Aerial Combat without the limiting camera of Auto Lock. In turn, Auto Lock is fully compatible with default Minecraft combat.

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/Pg6pFSPENSE" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>

</details>

<details>
<summary>Auto Lock Mode</summary>

- The "Auto Lock Mode" is toggleable (R by default) to keep the default Minecraft mechanics available when "Auto Lock Mode" is unfavorable. Text will show above the hotbar, indicating whether it is on or off. (Auto Lock: ON or Auto Lock: OFF)

- While "Auto Lock Mode" is enabled, the player will auto-face any entity they hit.

- "Auto Lock Mode" is independent of "Aerial Combat Mode" to allow players to use Aerial Combat without the limiting camera of Auto Lock. In turn, Auto Lock is fully compatible with default Minecraft combat.

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/TTTIoSHuTXI" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>

</details>

<details>
<summary>Movement</summary>

Aerial movement is essential in combos.

### Air Jump

- The player has infinite air jumps. This is the main way of moving in the air.

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/TBMlffpOA08" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>

### Dash

- The player has infinite dashes that boost the player in the direction they're looking. This is the easiest way to extend combos as the entity being attacked often gets out of reach while only using Air Jumps. Dashing is also the only consistent way to continue a combo after an Upper Attack.

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/ciI9zqUF1eM" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>
</details>

<details>
<summary>Attacks</summary>

While "Aerial Combat Mode" is enabled, most attacks send the hit entity upwards.

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/Y4Aew7L3m1A" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>

### Upper Attack

- This attack, executed by sprint-hitting an entity, deals an extra 2 damage and sends the hit entity further upwards, a little out of reach.

- This can be used to end a combo, letting the entity take fall damage, or to get extra height if the player can hit the entity before it falls.

- Particles will be emitted when the attack is done correctly.

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/mLnKoDI2fZE" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>

### Smash Attack

- This attack, executed by sneak-hitting an entity, deals an extra 4 damage and sends the hit entity down faster than falling.

- This is used to quickly end a combo as there usually isn't a way to continue hitting the entity post-attack. In return, the entity takes increased fall damage.

- Particles will be emitted when the attack is done correctly.

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/dY2_K8pRcgE" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>

</details>

You may add this mod to a modpack.

title: Deploy & Destroy
description: A simple mod that adds some useful tools and a few building blocks.
body:
## A collection of some useful tools, building blocks, and gameplay changes

### Deployer
Places blocks from its inventory.

### Destroyer
Breaks blocks and ejects their drops from its rear face.

### Detector
Emits a constant redstone signal when facing any opaque block

### Copper Pressure Plates
Only activated by players. Oxidize like other copper blocks. Can be waxed to halt oxidation progress.

### Upgradable Barrels
Copper, Iron, Gold, Diamond, and Netherite barrel tiers, each with additional storage. Upgrade with crafting recipes or in-place with associated upgrade items.

### Colored Redstone Lamps
A lamp for each dye color. Craft with dye or right-click with dye to change color.

### New Building Blocks
- Cracked and mossy brick variants, including stairs, slabs, and walls
- Mossy cobbled deepslate, including stairs, slabs, and walls
- Mossy deepslate bricks, including stairs, slabs, and walls
- Netherrack stairs, slabs, and walls
- Cut andesite, diorite, granite, and tuff, including slabs
- Grass bundles
- Charcoal blocks

### Blazing Coal
New fuel, crafted from blaze powder and coal. Smelts 4x as many items as coal.

### Nether Star Slab
Nether star slab

### Wrench
Right click on an orientable block to make it face toward you, or right click while sneaking to make it face away from you. \
Can be used by dispensers to make blocks face the same direction as the dispenser.

### In-World Sticky Piston Crafting
Right click a piston with a slime ball to convert it into a sticky piston.\
Scrape a sticky piston with an axe to convert it to a normal piston.

### Additional Useful Dispenser Behaviors
Dispensers can now:
- Scrape logs with axes
- Remove wax from waxed copper blocks with axes
- Lower copper oxidation levels with axes
- Empty/fill cauldrons with water, lava, and powdered snow
- Retrieve mushroom stew/suspicious stew from mooshrooms with bowls
- Feed flowers to brown mooshrooms to change their stew effects
- Cure villagers with golden apples

### Bucketable Striders
Striders can be picked with lava buckets.

### Additional Wandering Trader Trades
Glow berries have been added as a common trade.\
Sponges, wrenches, tadpole buckets, strider buckets, sniffer eggs, and mycelium have been added as rare trades.

### Shear Vines To Stop Growth
Vines will no longer grow after being sheared

### Loyalty Tridents Return From Void
Tridents with the loyalty enchantment will return to the player when thrown into the void.

### Deepslate Generators
Cobblestone and stone generators below y0 will now generate their respective deepslate variants.

### Deepslate Dungeons
Dungeons generated below y0 use cobbled deepslate and mossy cobbled deepslate instead of their cobblestone counterparts.

### Husk, Stray, and Bogged Dungeons
Dungeons may rarely generate with a husk, stray, or bogged spawner.

### Additional Farmable Materials
- Sand piles, dropped from husks, can be crafted into sand blocks
- Ice shards, dropped from strays, can be crafted into ice blocks
- Moss balls, dropped from bogged, can be crafted into moss blocks
- Quartz chunks, smelted from ghast tears, can be crafted into nether quartz

# FlagsLib

This mod is a Forge port of [PrideLib](https://github.com/Queerbric/pridelib).

FlagsLib is a small JIJ dependency for modders who want to use a centralized data-driven and configurable source of custom flags in their mods. FlagsLib can then be used to draw randomized graphical elements, or generate other colored visuals. FlagsLib lets flags be added through resource packs, optionally part of a mod. Flags used by FlagsLib can be configured either with resource packs, or a config file.
